anomalies.obs: On the Microcontroller sheet the USB-C receptacle VBUS pin (J5, pin A4) is wired to a junction that carries BOTH the green '+5V' power port and the red 'VBUS' global label. On the Power sheet 'VBUS' is the TPS2121RUXR (U7) OUT (pin 1) and '+5V' is its IN2 (pin 2). Because power ports and global labels of the same name share a net across sheets, this joins the mux input (+5V) directly to the mux output (VBUS) at the USB connector.
anomalies.expected: The spec states the mux output net 'VBUS' is 'distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux', and that U5 IN2 (USB +5V) and U5 OUT (VBUS) must be separate so the power mux can arbitrate between the barrel jack and USB.

evidence.quote: mcu.kicad_sch (sheet 3), top-right: J5 pin A4 tied to a node carrying both the '+5V' power symbol and the 'VBUS' global label
outputs a single OUT ... onto the VBUS net (the board's internal, unregulated/pre-buck rail — note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux)

anomalies.impact: Shorting the power-mux output to its USB input defeats the arbitration: when the 12 V barrel jack is present the mux OUT (≈12 V) is forced onto the USB VBUS pin, back-powering the host port (potential damage / spec violation), and IN2 is driven by OUT so the mux cannot switch or protect correctly.

parsed.summary: The drawing appears to merge the two power-mux nets: the USB-C VBUS pin (J5.A4) is connected to both the '+5V' (mux IN2) and 'VBUS' (mux OUT) labels, which the specification explicitly requires to be distinct, so the TPS2121 power mux is shorted input-to-output. No other deviation is supported with comparable confidence.
